sodium_driver_verdict.question: Does HP_FAT_SODIUM revive on its own with correct fat? Is BARI_SODIUM_CEREAL still needed?
sodium_driver_verdict.answer: PARTIAL REVIVAL — HP_FAT_SODIUM correctly fires on ONE product (7290106773714) with correct fat. However, the granola subpool has only 2 products with sodium >= 150mg. The graduated treatment (BARI_SODIUM_CEREAL=ON) adds a -5pt penalty to the 394mg salted product (no grade move, still C) and -2pt to the 195mg product (already D, no grade move). On CLEAN DATA, BARI_SODIUM_CEREAL has NO grade movers in the granola subpool.
sodium_driver_verdict.recommendation: DO NOT ACTIVATE BARI_SODIUM_CEREAL for the granola subpool at this time. Reasons: (1) 0 grade movers in Pass A→B; (2) HP_FAT_SODIUM already fires correctly on the salted product; (3) the sodium concern was driven by the full cereals corpus (63 products), not granola-only; (4) activating BARI_SODIUM_CEREAL adds 2 small score penalties with no grade impact, adding maintenance cost for no consumer-visible benefit on granola. The flag remains available for the full cereals corpus if the sodium scoring decision is revisited for that pool.
sodium_driver_verdict.scope_guard: BARI_SODIUM_CEREAL is scoped to snack_bar_granola + cereal. This analysis covers ONLY granola. The verdict applies to the granola display page. The full cereals corpus (which has cornflakes at 600mg, muesli at 400mg) may warrant separate D7 review.
sodium_driver_verdict.live_page_impact: The 7 grade movers from Pass A vs live frontend are due to ENGINE EVOLUTION, not the sodium flag. They represent the delta between old engine (2026-06-15 traces) and current engine. These are REAL score moves that must be disclosed to Product Agent before any frontend update.
